claims.title: Hominins leave footprints at Laetoli
claims.summary: Early hominins, attributed to Australopithecus afarensis, cross a layer of fresh volcanic ash near Laetoli; their footprints harden and survive, giving direct evidence of upright walking.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Tanzania: From the footprints of Laetoli and the gold of Kilwa to Nyerere's union and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/TZA/chronicle#ev-3600000bce-hominins-leave-footprints-at-laetoli, claim TL:TZA:event:3600000bce:hominins-leave-footprints-at-laetoli, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Homo habilis and Oldowan tools at Olduvai
claims.summary: Early members of the genus Homo at Olduvai Gorge make simple flaked-pebble tools of the Oldowan industry, among the earliest manufactured implements known.

sources.label: Palaeoanthropological Sites of Human Evolution: Laetoli–Olduvai Gorge

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Tanzania: From the footprints of Laetoli and the gold of Kilwa to Nyerere's union and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/TZA/chronicle#ev-1800000bce-homo-habilis-and-oldowan-tools-at-olduvai, claim TL:TZA:event:1800000bce:homo-habilis-and-oldowan-tools-at-olduvai, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mary Leakey finds the Zinjanthropus skull
claims.summary: At Olduvai Gorge, Mary Leakey uncovers the robust hominin skull OH 5 (Zinjanthropus / Paranthropus boisei), a landmark in the study of human evolution.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Tanzania: From the footprints of Laetoli and the gold of Kilwa to Nyerere's union and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/TZA/chronicle#ev-1959-mary-leakey-finds-the-zinjanthropus-skull, claim TL:TZA:event:1959:mary-leakey-finds-the-zinjanthropus-skull, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Discovery of the Laetoli footprints
claims.summary: Mary Leakey's team excavates the trail of 3.6-million-year-old hominin footprints at Laetoli, confirming early bipedalism and cementing Tanzania's place in human prehistory.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Tanzania: From the footprints of Laetoli and the gold of Kilwa to Nyerere's union and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/TZA/chronicle#ev-1976-discovery-of-the-laetoli-footprints, claim TL:TZA:event:1976:discovery-of-the-laetoli-footprints, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bantu farmers reach the coast
claims.summary: Iron-using Bantu-speaking farmers settle the Tanzanian coast and interior, part of the wider Bantu expansion that reshaped eastern and southern Africa.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Tanzania: From the footprints of Laetoli and the gold of Kilwa to Nyerere's union and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/TZA/chronicle#ev-500bce-bantu-farmers-reach-the-coast, claim TL:TZA:event:500bce:bantu-farmers-reach-the-coast, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rise of the Swahili coast
claims.summary: Coastal communities trading across the Indian Ocean develop the Swahili language and an Afro-Islamic urban culture, founding settlements that grow into trading city-states.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Tanzania: From the footprints of Laetoli and the gold of Kilwa to Nyerere's union and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/TZA/chronicle#ev-800-rise-of-the-swahili-coast, claim TL:TZA:event:800:rise-of-the-swahili-coast, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Shirazi dynasty founds Kilwa
claims.summary: According to the Kilwa Chronicle, the Shirazi line founds the ruling house of Kilwa Kisiwani; the city begins its rise as a Swahili trading power.

sources.label: Ruins of Kilwa Kisiwani and Ruins of Songo Mnara

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Tanzania: From the footprints of Laetoli and the gold of Kilwa to Nyerere's union and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/TZA/chronicle#ev-1100-shirazi-dynasty-founds-kilwa, claim TL:TZA:event:1100:shirazi-dynasty-founds-kilwa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kilwa dominates the gold trade
claims.summary: Controlling the gold exported through Sofala, Kilwa reaches its peak of wealth, minting coins and building the Great Mosque, the largest in the region.

sources.label: Ruins of Kilwa Kisiwani and Ruins of Songo Mnara
Kilwa, the abandoned East African city that controlled the medieval gold trade

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Tanzania: From the footprints of Laetoli and the gold of Kilwa to Nyerere's union and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/TZA/chronicle#ev-1300-kilwa-dominates-the-gold-trade, claim TL:TZA:event:1300:kilwa-dominates-the-gold-trade, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ibn Battuta visits Kilwa
claims.summary: The traveller Ibn Battuta describes Kilwa as a prosperous, devout and beautifully built Muslim city, attesting to the wealth of the medieval Swahili coast.

sources.label: Ruins of Kilwa Kisiwani and Ruins of Songo Mnara

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Tanzania: From the footprints of Laetoli and the gold of Kilwa to Nyerere's union and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/TZA/chronicle#ev-1331-ibn-battuta-visits-kilwa, claim TL:TZA:event:1331:ibn-battuta-visits-kilwa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Vasco da Gama reaches the coast
claims.summary: The Portuguese navigator Vasco da Gama arrives on the East African coast en route to India, opening an era of Portuguese intrusion that disrupted the Swahili city-states.

sources.label: Portuguese conquest of the East African coast

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Tanzania: From the footprints of Laetoli and the gold of Kilwa to Nyerere's union and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/TZA/chronicle#ev-1498-vasco-da-gama-reaches-the-coast, claim TL:TZA:event:1498:vasco-da-gama-reaches-the-coast, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Said bin Sultan moves his capital to Zanzibar
claims.summary: The Omani ruler Said bin Sultan transfers his capital from Muscat to Zanzibar, making the islands the commercial heart of the western Indian Ocean.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Tanzania: From the footprints of Laetoli and the gold of Kilwa to Nyerere's union and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/TZA/chronicle#ev-1840-said-bin-sultan-moves-his-capital-to-zanzibar, claim TL:TZA:event:1840:said-bin-sultan-moves-his-capital-to-zanzibar, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Clove plantations and the caravan trade
claims.summary: Zanzibar and Pemba become the world's leading clove producers, while caravans reaching to Lake Tanganyika feed a vast and brutal trade in enslaved people and ivory.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Tanzania: From the footprints of Laetoli and the gold of Kilwa to Nyerere's union and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/TZA/chronicle#ev-1840-clove-plantations-and-the-caravan-trade, claim TL:TZA:event:1840:clove-plantations-and-the-caravan-trade, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Zanzibar becomes a separate sultanate
claims.summary: On Said's death his domains are divided; his son Majid becomes the first sultan of Zanzibar, separating the islands from Oman.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Tanzania: From the footprints of Laetoli and the gold of Kilwa to Nyerere's union and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/TZA/chronicle#ev-1856-zanzibar-becomes-a-separate-sultanate, claim TL:TZA:event:1856:zanzibar-becomes-a-separate-sultanate, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Zanzibar bans the seaborne slave trade
claims.summary: Under British pressure Sultan Barghash signs a treaty prohibiting the maritime slave trade and closing the Stone Town slave market, though domestic slavery endures for decades.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Tanzania: From the footprints of Laetoli and the gold of Kilwa to Nyerere's union and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/TZA/chronicle#ev-1873-zanzibar-bans-the-seaborne-slave-trade, claim TL:TZA:event:1873:zanzibar-bans-the-seaborne-slave-trade, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Germany establishes German East Africa
claims.summary: Following Carl Peters's treaties, the German government charters his company, founding the colony of German East Africa over the Tanzanian mainland and the Great Lakes territories.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Tanzania: From the footprints of Laetoli and the gold of Kilwa to Nyerere's union and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/TZA/chronicle#ev-1885-germany-establishes-german-east-africa, claim TL:TZA:event:1885:germany-establishes-german-east-africa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Maji Maji rebellion
claims.summary: Inspired by the prophet Kinjikitile Ngwale, southern peoples rise against German rule, forced labour and cotton-growing; the revolt spreads widely before being crushed.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Tanzania: From the footprints of Laetoli and the gold of Kilwa to Nyerere's union and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/TZA/chronicle#ev-1905-maji-maji-rebellion, claim TL:TZA:event:1905:maji-maji-rebellion, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Scorched earth and the Great Hunger
claims.summary: German forces suppress the rebellion by destroying crops and villages; the ensuing famine kills tens to hundreds of thousands of people, a catastrophe scholars term genocidal.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Tanzania: From the footprints of Laetoli and the gold of Kilwa to Nyerere's union and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/TZA/chronicle#ev-1906-scorched-earth-and-the-great-hunger, claim TL:TZA:event:1906:scorched-earth-and-the-great-hunger, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Tanganyika becomes a British mandate
claims.summary: After the First World War the Treaty of Versailles strips Germany of the colony; Britain administers the mainland as the Tanganyika Territory under a League of Nations mandate from 1922.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Tanzania: From the footprints of Laetoli and the gold of Kilwa to Nyerere's union and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/TZA/chronicle#ev-1919-tanganyika-becomes-a-british-mandate, claim TL:TZA:event:1919:tanganyika-becomes-a-british-mandate, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of TANU
claims.summary: Julius Nyerere builds the Tanganyika African National Union, which campaigns for independence by constitutional means and comes to dominate the territory's politics.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Tanzania: From the footprints of Laetoli and the gold of Kilwa to Nyerere's union and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/TZA/chronicle#ev-1954-founding-of-tanu, claim TL:TZA:event:1954:founding-of-tanu, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Tanganyika gains independence
claims.summary: Mainland Tanganyika becomes independent from Britain under Nyerere and TANU; it becomes a republic with Nyerere as president on 9 December 1962.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Tanzania: From the footprints of Laetoli and the gold of Kilwa to Nyerere's union and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/TZA/chronicle#ev-1961-tanganyika-gains-independence, claim TL:TZA:event:1961:tanganyika-gains-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Zanzibar Revolution
claims.summary: The African majority overthrows the Arab-led sultanate of Zanzibar in a bloody uprising, establishing a republic under Abeid Karume.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Tanzania: From the footprints of Laetoli and the gold of Kilwa to Nyerere's union and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/TZA/chronicle#ev-1964-zanzibar-revolution, claim TL:TZA:event:1964:zanzibar-revolution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Union of Tanganyika and Zanzibar
claims.summary: Tanganyika and Zanzibar unite to form the United Republic of Tanzania, with Nyerere as president and Karume as vice-president; Zanzibar keeps its own government.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Tanzania: From the footprints of Laetoli and the gold of Kilwa to Nyerere's union and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/TZA/chronicle#ev-1964-union-of-tanganyika-and-zanzibar, claim TL:TZA:event:1964:union-of-tanganyika-and-zanzibar, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Arusha Declaration
claims.summary: Nyerere proclaims Ujamaa, committing Tanzania to socialism and self-reliance, nationalising key sectors and launching the policy of collective villages.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Tanzania: From the footprints of Laetoli and the gold of Kilwa to Nyerere's union and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/TZA/chronicle#ev-1967-the-arusha-declaration, claim TL:TZA:event:1967:the-arusha-declaration, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Nyerere steps down
claims.summary: Julius Nyerere voluntarily retires from the presidency, handing power to Ali Hassan Mwinyi in a peaceful transition and opening the way to economic liberalisation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Tanzania: From the footprints of Laetoli and the gold of Kilwa to Nyerere's union and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/TZA/chronicle#ev-1985-nyerere-steps-down, claim TL:TZA:event:1985:nyerere-steps-down, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Return to multiparty politics
claims.summary: Tanzania amends its constitution to permit multiple parties, ending decades of one-party rule; the first multiparty elections follow in 1995.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Tanzania: From the footprints of Laetoli and the gold of Kilwa to Nyerere's union and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/TZA/chronicle#ev-1992-return-to-multiparty-politics, claim TL:TZA:event:1992:return-to-multiparty-politics, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Dodoma confirmed as capital
claims.summary: Tanzania advances the long-planned move of its capital to the central city of Dodoma, while Dar es Salaam remains the largest city and commercial centre.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Tanzania: From the footprints of Laetoli and the gold of Kilwa to Nyerere's union and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/TZA/chronicle#ev-1996-dodoma-confirmed-as-capital, claim TL:TZA:event:1996:dodoma-confirmed-as-capital, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Samia Suluhu Hassan becomes president
claims.summary: On the death of President John Magufuli, Vice-President Samia Suluhu Hassan is sworn in as the first female president of the United Republic of Tanzania.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Tanzania: From the footprints of Laetoli and the gold of Kilwa to Nyerere's union and a modern East African republic.", terralore.co/country/TZA/chronicle#ev-2021-samia-suluhu-hassan-becomes-president, claim TL:TZA:event:2021:samia-suluhu-hassan-becomes-president, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
